AcceptRequest.description:
The code a sign-up asks for, when joining an entrant by a member's
invite needs one.
AcceptRequest.title: AcceptRequest

AcceptedInvite.description:
What accepting an invite did: the invite as it stands now, and, for a
place in a contest, the entrant the caller is in now, null for a role.
AcceptedInvite.title: AcceptedInvite

Account.description:
Someone with their email, as they see themself and as the organisers
of a contest they registered for see them.
Account.title: Account

Announcement.description:
One announcement: where it is, by the names of its contest and task,
its number there, what it says, when it was posted, whether it is
closed, whether it answers a question, and, for an organiser, which.
Announcement.title: Announcement

AnnouncementLink.description:
The announcement a message names: on the question's contest, or on
the task of it named `task`, by its number there, and its `title` as
the message names it, so a page writes the message with the title as
the link; none when the message no longer reads as the platform wrote
it, edited at the forge.
AnnouncementLink.title: AnnouncementLink

AnnouncementRequest.description: An announcement's title and text, as posted or as edited.
AnnouncementRequest.title: AnnouncementRequest

AnsweredQuestion.description:
The clarification an announcement answers: whose desk it is in, the
asking entrant's `entrant.<id>`, and the question's number there.
AnsweredQuestion.title: AnsweredQuestion

Better.description: Which way a number is better, as the program that makes it says.
Better.title: Better

Block.description:
A block a value or a column may use: the `name` a node gives as `block`, what it
gives in words, and its forms. A block with more than one form, such as
`min`, means the one its node's inputs fit.
Block.title: Block

BlockForm.description:
One way a block is given its inputs: what it is `given`, in words,
such as "numbers" or "a group's runs", its inputs by name, in the order
a node writes them, where it may be used, `scope`, a task's value, a
leaderboard's column or both, and what it `gives`: a number, one
submission's results, or, for `otherwise`, either.
BlockForm.title: BlockForm

BlockInput.description:
One input of a form: the `kind` it takes, a number, a group's `runs`,
a task's `results`, one `submission`'s results, `either` a number or a
submission's results, `best_each`'s value by `name` and its
`directions`, `weights` by a repeated input's values, what a missing
report or input counts as, a `path`, a folder of the task such as
`programs/mean/`, or a `language`, one of the catalogue's `languages`;
a list of at least
`least` and at most `most` when `least` is given (`most` null for no
most), one node otherwise; whether it may be left out; whether its
block reads it once for each run or result it goes over (`per_run`),
as a fold's `of` and `where` and a pick's `where` and `by` are; and
whether it takes a number written out alone, never a leaf or a block
(`plain`).
BlockInput.title: BlockInput

BoxInput.description: One input of a run workflow drawn as a box.
BoxInput.title: BoxInput

BoxOutput.description:
One output of a run workflow drawn as a box. `type` and a number's
meaning are null while the port is not known. A port carries no title
and no unit.
BoxOutput.title: BoxOutput

CallbackAnswer.description: Where the grading stands once its run's report is taken.
CallbackAnswer.title: CallbackAnswer

CancelRequest.description: Why staff end the submission, a sentence its contestant reads.
CancelRequest.title: CancelRequest

Catalogue.description:
Everything a value's or a column's tree may be made of. `blocks` in
the catalogue's order. `leaves` the keys a task's value writes a leaf
with, each alone in its mapping: `{runs: <group>}` a group's runs, for
a fold's `over`; `{run: [<group>, <column>]}` that column of each run,
inside a fold over that group; `{value: <name>}` another of the task's
values; and `{fact: <name>}` one of `facts`, a fact of the submission.
`leaderboard_leaves` those a leaderboard's column writes: `{results: <task>}`
a task's results; `{value: [<task, pick column or block>, <value or
fact>]}` a value or fact of a submission, the task's own read only
inside `where`, `by` or a fold's `of`; `{column: <name>}` or `{column:
[<leaderboard>, <name>]}` another column; and `best_each`'s `{name: <value>}`.
`leaderboard_facts` the facts a column may read of a submission. A number is
a leaf too. `skip` is what a block's `missing` says to leave out a run
whose report is missing, or a submission whose input is missing,
which otherwise makes a pick, fold or `best_each` missing; a number
there counts as that number.
`languages` are those an `exec` block's program may be written in.
Catalogue.title: Catalogue

CellDiff.description:
One displayed cell of a row, its number before the regrade and
after, exactly, null where it was or is missing, its text before and
after, null where it had none, and the submissions the cell after
leaves out as still waiting, as the leaderboard does.
CellDiff.title: CellDiff

Change.description:
One entry of a place's history: the version it made, who made it, what
they said about it and when. `author` is the username of `author_id`,
which the history names whether or not they still hold a role there, and
none when the forge knows no such account, the change has no author, or
the platform made it, which is no person (a new task's first files).
Change.title: Change

ChangeKind.description: What a regrade did to one submission, as the module says.
ChangeKind.title: ChangeKind

CheckDefinition.description:
A `workflow.yaml` to check as a version would be, writing nothing.
`owner` and `name`, when both are given, name the workflow this text is
a draft of, so a draft that would hold that workflow is refused.
CheckDefinition.title: CheckDefinition

CheckRun.description:
One run of a check as its save graded it: its `id`, its `key` as
the plan gives it, its `verdict` and the numbers its steps reported,
exactly.
CheckRun.title: CheckRun

Checked.description:
Every problem a version would be refused for; none means it would be
made.
Checked.title: Checked

Clarification.description:
One question: its contest by name, whose desk it is in, the asking
entrant's `entrant.<id>`, its number there, the task it names, what it
asks, when, whether it is answered and whether it is open, and every
message under it, oldest first.
Clarification.title: Clarification

Closed.description:
Why a task is not open to a row, the first of these that applies; and,
to a person who holds no approved row, `not_approved` where it is
otherwise open, as a submit would be refused.
Closed.title: Closed

CommentRequest.description:
One message under a question: a contestant's follow-up or an
organiser's reply.
CommentRequest.title: CommentRequest

ContestHome.description:
A contest's home for the caller. `organises` says the caller holds a
role at the contest, which keeps them from registering; `registration`
is their registration panel, as `entrants/mine` answers it: their
entrant, whether and how they may register, and whether to ask them for
a code. `standing` is their own row of each leaderboard they read, as
that leaderboard's route shows it to them, empty unless they are in an
approved entrant.
ContestHome.title: ContestHome

ContestNames.description: A contest by the names of its org and itself.
ContestNames.title: ContestNames

ContestSummary.description:
A contest the caller sees, with its title, when it runs, who sees it,
and the status of the caller's entrant, null when they are in none.
ContestSummary.title: ContestSummary

ContestVisibility.description:
Who sees the contest at all: anyone, guests included; anyone signed
in; or only its contestants and organisers.
ContestVisibility.title: ContestVisibility

CopyWorkflow.description:
A copy to make of `source`, `<owner>/<name>@<version>`, as `name`
under `owner`, which follows the rule for making one.
CopyWorkflow.title: CopyWorkflow

Counted.description: A submission a cell counted or left out, by its task and number.
Counted.title: Counted

CountedBy.description:
A leaderboard's cell that counted a submission: the leaderboard's key and the
column's name.
CountedBy.title: CountedBy

CreateContest.description: A contest to make, titled `title` or, without one, its name.
CreateContest.title: CreateContest

CreateTask.description: A task to make, titled `title` or, without one, its name.
CreateTask.title: CreateTask

CreateVersion.description:
A name to freeze the saved draft under, `v` and a whole number from
1 with no leading zero, such as `v1` or `v10`, and the token
the caller saved it with, so the version is of that save; with none, of
whatever is saved now. `revision` also checks that the files have not moved.
CreateVersion.title: CreateVersion

CreateWorkflow.description:
A workflow to make under `owner`: the caller's own username, or the
name of an org where they hold the manager role or above.
CreateWorkflow.title: CreateWorkflow

DeclaredInput.description:
One input a workflow declares, as the task form shows it: its id, its
type, its options on an enum, whether a task may leave it out, and the
title, line of help and unit the workflow gives the organiser for it,
each none when it gives none. Who gives it, and whether it repeats, are
the task's (SIMPLER-CORE.md 8), so the form reads each as given once by
the task until it says. A workflow gives no defaults: an entrant input's
`default` is the task's, in `task.yaml`.
DeclaredInput.title: DeclaredInput

Definition.description:
A `workflow.yaml` as text, and the token a save of it carries back:
none for one that is not there yet. `revision` names the saved repository,
including its files, for publishing exactly that save.
Definition.title: Definition

DefinitionError.description:
One thing wrong with a definition file: its YAML path, "" for the file
as a whole, and a sentence a form shows beside that field.
DefinitionError.title: DefinitionError

DefinitionProblem.description:
One problem: its YAML path in `workflow.yaml`, `steps[1].with.binary`,
and what is wrong there. The path is empty for the file as a whole.
`step` is the flat step a problem inside a box belongs to, when the path
can only name the box; none otherwise.
DefinitionProblem.title: DefinitionProblem

Draft.description:
A save kept as a draft: the version its files were written as, the
errors that kept it from publishing, and what it held back.
Draft.title: Draft

EnterMarkRequest.description:
A mark for one of a submission's values that reads an `entered`
block: the value's name, and the mark written out as a plain decimal,
such as `7.5`, as text so it stays exact. Null or "" clears the mark.
The forge checks a mark against the bounds the task's live version
gives, and does not read them when the mark is cleared.
EnterMarkRequest.title: EnterMarkRequest

Entered.description:
What accepting a place in a contest did: the entrant the caller is in
now, its status, and whether accepting `made` it, `joined` it, or found
them in it `already`.
Entered.title: Entered

EnteredMark.description:
A mark as it was kept: the value, the mark as the plain decimal it
counts as, or null when it was cleared, the user id of who entered it,
and when. Every mark entered is kept, a clear included, and the latest
is the value's.
EnteredMark.title: EnteredMark

Entrant.description: An entrant as its members read it, with its members.
Entrant.title: Entrant

EntrantRef.description: An entrant by its id and the name it is shown under.
EntrantRef.title: EntrantRef

ExtensionRequest.description:
How long, in seconds, the extension moves the due and the close of
each of the contest's `tasks`, by name, or of every task when it names
none, in place of any extension there was.
ExtensionRequest.title: ExtensionRequest

FailedCheck.description:
A check that refused its save, for the task's organisers: its
`index` in `checks`, from 1; why it failed, a sentence each, at most
20; its `runs`; the `outcomes` of its steps done once, and of its batch
steps the outcome given once for all their runs (`compile_error`, else
`accepted`), by step; the
number each value's program reported, exactly, or its text, by value;
and the fault of its steps, null when none. Entrants never read a
check.
FailedCheck.title: FailedCheck

FeedEntry.description:
One grading among a task's or a contest's: the grading as an
organiser reads it, its task by name, null for a task the platform has
no name for, its `label`, the letter of its place in the contest's
`tasks`, null once the contest no longer lists it or its settings do
not read, and `by`, whose submission it is: the `entrant` by its id and
`entrant_name`, the name it is shown under, and the member who
submitted it by `user_id` and `username`, both null when a reconcile
found it at the forge, the username null when the forge did not say.
FeedEntry.title: FeedEntry

FileChange.description:
One file of a save, with the token it was read with: typed as
`content`, uploaded for this path as `upload`, or removed with `remove:
true`, exactly one of the three. The token is null for a file the save
creates, and a removal always carries one. Removing a folder, such as a
test, is removing each file under it, named one by one.
FileChange.title: FileChange

FileContent.description:
One file at one version, with the token a write presents back, and
`upload` when it is a file an organiser uploaded: its `content` is then
the pointer to the bytes, never opened as text, and `upload` the size
and SHA-256 of what it holds. A typed file has none. `version` is the
commit holding the file as read, the latest change to it or the one it
was read at, which a task's file is downloaded at
(`/-/downloads/<org>/<contest>/<task>/versions/<version>/<path>`); null
when the forge names no commit and it was not read at one. A tree's
entries name their `version` the same way.
FileContent.title: FileContent

ForgeUrl.description:
Where a browser reaches the forge's own pages: sign-in and the account
settings. No trailing slash.
ForgeUrl.title: ForgeUrl

Grading.description:
One grading as an organiser managing its task reads it: the submission
by its number, the publication it grades against, its attempt and
whether that is the submission's `latest`, the one staff cancel or
retry, the member who submitted it, `submitted_by`, null when a
reconcile found it at the forge, where it stands, the reason it failed,
the sentence staff cancelled it with, its result, its times, and whether
the platform made it by itself, `automatic`, retrying the attempt before
it once that failed.

On a latest attempt that has not finished with a result, still being
graded, a system error or staff cancelled, `last_good` is the latest
earlier attempt that did, the one its submission counts meanwhile on
the leaderboards and to its contestant; null on any other, and when no
attempt has a result.

An attempt that is `over_limit` was made to grade a delayed submission
again and ended at once, run by nothing, since its entrant had no room
left under the task's most submissions: `limit` is that most, null on
every other status. On a latest attempt of a submission with no result
that reads as `system_error` or `over_limit`, `retry_limit` is the
task's most when a retry now would end over the limit, so the retry's
confirmation says so before it runs ("Not graded: the entrant has
reached the limit of 10 submissions for this task."); null otherwise,
when a retry would grade it. `regrade` is the regrade of many the
attempt belongs to, null for none; `change`, given only on the feed read
by `regrade`, what that regrade did to the submission.

A submission is graded by up to two pipelines, each with attempts of
its own: `early`, the runs shown during the contest, and `late`, the
rest, made once the early one is done, with `early` naming the early
attempt it follows, null on an early one. Its `result` is a
`RunsResult`.
Grading.title: Grading

GradingStatus.description:
Where one grading stands. `queued` waits for its run to be started,
which happens as soon as the request that made it commits; `dispatched`
is held by the CI, waiting for a machine or checking out; `running` has
had a step ask for its job. It ends `done` with a result,
`system_error`, a grading that failed for a reason of the platform's,
never a grade: its run could not be started, or did not report before
its deadline; `cancelled`, by staff ending one in `system_error`, or
by a rejudge replacing one still being graded; or `over_limit`, made to
grade a delayed submission again and ended at once, run by nothing,
since its entrant had no room left under the task's `submissions.max`.
GradingStatus.title: GradingStatus

Grant.description:
What an invite gives once accepted: an organiser's place in a contest,
which registers the person or puts them in the entrant it names, and
lets them in by the contest's invite way; a member's place in their
entrant, asked by one of its members; or one of the organiser roles at
the invite's scope.
Grant.title: Grant

GrantRequest.description:
Give the named user `role` at the scope, moving them from any other
role they hold directly there.
GrantRequest.title: GrantRequest

Header.description:
One displayed column, the same for every row: its `name`, the
`decimals` it is shown to, null when the leaderboard gives none, the least and
most it can give, both null unless both are known, and each
self-reported value it reads, which a page marks on the column's
header.
Header.title: Header

HeldRole.description: A role the user holds, at the org, contest or task `names` reaches.
HeldRole.title: HeldRole

HoldRequest.description:
Ending the contest's hold early. Without `confirm` nothing changes,
and the answer is `confirmation_required` with the words to show.
HoldRequest.title: HoldRequest

HoldState.description:
Where the contest's hold stands: its `from` and `until`, a time or
`staff`, both null with no hold; whether it holds now; and, once staff
ended it early, who, by user id and username, null when the forge gives
none, and when.
HoldState.title: HoldState

Holder.description:
Someone holding `role` at the scope asked about, held directly at
`at_names`: that scope, or a broader one, such as the org of a contest
whose admin is listed at the contest.
Holder.title: Holder

InputField.description:
One input the contestant gives, with what its form shows: its
`type`, its `label`, the task's, else its key, the `options` of an enum,
the `default` a value takes when it is left out, `min` and `max` of a
number, exactly, `max_size`, the most its files may total in bytes, and
`parts`, on an input given once per tuple. A number input's default is
served as its exact digits, as its bounds are. The submit panel shows
one field or drop zone per input.
InputField.title: InputField

InputPart.description:
One part of an input given once per tuple: the tuple's title, and the
most that part may hold, in bytes.
InputPart.title: InputPart

Invitation.description:
One of the caller's own invites into an entrant of the contest, still
waiting: the invite, the entrant, whether an organiser sent it, and when
it lapses.
Invitation.title: Invitation

Invite.description:
An invite: where it is to, by its names, and the title of the contest
it is at or under, null at an org; what it grants, a place in a
contest (`contestant`), a member's place in an entrant (`member`) or an
organiser role, the entrant it asks someone into, if any, the username
or the address it names, who sent it, where it stands, whether it has
lapsed, its dates, and what became of its mail: `waiting`, `sent`,
`failed`, or `off` where the deployment sends no mail.
Invite.title: Invite

InviteRequest.description:
Who to invite, by exactly one of `username` and `email`, to what, for
how many days the invite stands, 14 unless given, and, for a place in a
contest, the `entrant` it puts them straight into, by its id, or none to
register them on their own. A member's place in an entrant is offered by
the entrant's members, never here.
InviteRequest.title: InviteRequest

InvitedIn.description:
An invite into an entrant still waiting: its id, the username or the
address it names, who sent it, whether an organiser sent it, and when it
lapses.
InvitedIn.title: InvitedIn

Leaderboard.description:
One leaderboard as the caller reads it: the headers of the columns listed
to them, the keys its rows were sorted by and the sort keys `dropped`,
hidden on a row served or not listed, its rows cut to its audience, and
`held_from`, when the hold holds other rows from, null when it holds
nothing for the caller.
Leaderboard.title: Leaderboard

LeaderboardAudience.description:
Who a leaderboard is for: `staff`, `entrants` or `everyone`, and which
`rows` they are given: `all`, `own`, or a number of top rows.
LeaderboardAudience.title: LeaderboardAudience

LeaderboardCell.description:
One listed column of a row: its `number`, null when missing, hidden,
waiting or text; its `text`, null when it is a number or missing;
whether it is `hidden` from the caller, having read
something they are not shown, told only on the caller's own row and to
staff and false elsewhere; the submissions it counted; and those it
left out as still waiting, both null unless the row is the caller's
own or they are staff.
LeaderboardCell.title: LeaderboardCell

LeaderboardDiff.description:
One leaderboard that reads the regraded task, directly or through another
leaderboard's column, as staff read it, every row and cell and no hold: its
key and title, its displayed columns' headers as they stand after, the
columns it sorts by, and each row in its order after the regrade;
`unread` with no rows when the publication the results counted under
before no longer reads, so there is nothing to compare.
LeaderboardDiff.title: LeaderboardDiff

LeaderboardRow.description:
A row on the leaderboard: its place, shared by rows equal on every sort
key, null on a leaderboard with no `sort`, when a sort key was dropped for
the caller, and on a leaderboard showing them only their own row; whose it
is; its listed cells in order; `held`, how many of its submissions
the hold keeps from the caller; and `grading`, how many of its
submissions to the tasks the leaderboard reads still grade, a value the
caller is shown still to come, null unless the row is the caller's
own or they are staff.
LeaderboardRow.title: LeaderboardRow

LeaderboardRowOwner.description:
Whose a row is: an entrant by its id, and the name it is shown under,
its own or its member's username, empty when the forge gives none.
LeaderboardRowOwner.title: LeaderboardRowOwner

LimitSource.description:
A container limit raised to `n * scale + add` when that is more,
`scale` and `add` exactly as the declaration writes them, `n` read
from exactly one of `input`, a number input; `sum`, the sum of a number
input over every program of a programs port, `<port>.<input>`; and
`max`, the largest of one. The other two are null.
LimitSource.title: LimitSource

ListedContest.description:
A contest in its org's list, by name, with its state, start and end as
its settings say them, all three null when its settings cannot be read.
ListedContest.title: ListedContest

Locks.description:
When an entrant's roster locks: at the contest's start, or at the
entrant's first submission.
Locks.title: Locks

MailStatus.description:
What became of an invite's mail: `waiting` until it is handed to the
mail server, `sent` once it took it, `failed` when it could not be sent,
the server refusing, not answering, or there being no address to send it
to, and `off` where the deployment has no mail server. A mail still
`waiting` minutes on was cut short by a restart, and is sent again from
the invite.
MailStatus.title: MailStatus

Marks.description:
The marks the caller's row holds on a task, for a leaderboard reading which
of its submissions an entrant marks: the numbers of the submissions
marked, the most it may hold, and the row's close on the task, after
which they are frozen.
Marks.title: Marks

Me.description:
The signed-in user and their roles at every scope. `degraded` is set
when the forge did not answer and the identity comes from the session.
Me.title: Me

Member.description:
Someone in an entrant: their id, who they are, null once their account
is gone, the way they came in by, `invite`, `signup` or `organiser`, that
way's name, if it has one, and when they joined.
Member.title: Member

MemberInviteRequest.description:
Who to ask into the caller's entrant, by exactly one of `username` and
`email`.
MemberInviteRequest.title: MemberInviteRequest

Message.description:
One message under a question: whether the asker wrote it, what it
says, when, and, on the message a public answer leaves, the
announcement it was answered in.
Message.title: Message

MoveRequest.description: The entrant of the same contest to move the member to, by its id.
MoveRequest.title: MoveRequest

MyEntry.description:
The caller's registration panel: their entrant, if any, their own
invites into the contest's entrants, whether the registration window is
open, whether they can register and, when they cannot, why; whether to
ask them for a code, true only when a code would let them in; and the
contest's sizes, the most and the fewest people in an entrant, and when
an entrant's roster locks, at the `start` or at its `first_submission`.
MyEntry.title: MyEntry

Named.description: An org, a contest or a task, by the name people call it.
Named.title: Named

NotReady.description:
Deliberately not a problem document: an orchestrator reads the status in
a fixed place. What failed underneath is in the log and not here.
NotReady.title: NotReady

OnceReports.description:
What the steps done once reported, and what a batch step gives once
for all its runs: numbers, exactly, and texts; and the outcome each
returned, by its id, which the `compiled` fact reads: for a batch step,
the outcome it gives once for all its runs, `compile_error`, else
`accepted` whatever its runs ended.
OnceReports.title: OnceReports

OnceShown.description:
What a grading's steps done once reported, and what a batch step
gives once for all its runs, as its reader is shown it: numbers,
exactly, and texts, the compile log among them; for an entrant, only
the reports `show` lists, by name.
OnceShown.title: OnceShown

OpenInviteRequest.description: The token after the `#` of the link an invite's mail carried.
OpenInviteRequest.title: OpenInviteRequest

OrgProfile.description:
An org's own fields at the forge, which its admin changes: the name it
is shown under, none while it has none of its own, and its description.
OrgProfile.title: OrgProfile

OrganisedEntrant.description:
An entrant as the contest's organisers read it, its members with
their email.
OrganisedEntrant.title: OrganisedEntrant

OrganisedMember.description: A member as the contest's organisers read them, with their email.
OrganisedMember.title: OrganisedMember

OrganisedResult.description:
A submission's grading as organisers read it beside the grading
itself: the payload its contestant reads, with everything filled in as
once the task has revealed. `status` is the grading's own, as in the
gradings routes. Every value and run is there at once, each value with
when it shows and what it read, and `facts` holds `seconds_late`,
`seconds` and `compiled` as the values read them.
OrganisedResult.title: OrganisedResult

OrganisedSubmission.description:
One submission of an entrant, as organisers read it: its number
among the entrant's, when it was taken, and its grading with everything
filled in.
OrganisedSubmission.title: OrganisedSubmission

Person.description:
Someone as another person sees them, by their forge id. Their email
stays out.
Person.title: Person

Primitive.description:
One version of a primitive, `ref` being what a step's `use:` names.
Its declaration is in `title` and `description`, what the editor shows
of it, and in `batch`, `network`, `limits`, `limits_from`, `inputs` and
`outputs`, or in `forms` when the primitive declares several and those
four stay empty; a version in a format the platform no longer reads has
none of them and `problem` instead, so no step uses it.
Primitive.title: Primitive

PrimitiveForm.description:
One way to use a primitive that declares several. The editor shows
`description`; the ports and limits are what a step of this form gives
and takes. Nothing here is the step's choice of form: the save picks it.
PrimitiveForm.title: PrimitiveForm

PrimitivePort.description:
One port: its type, the options an enum takes, the names a
`named_files` port's files must have, whether it may be left out, on an
input whether the primitive runs what arrives there and whether it
keeps it from the program it runs, on a `number` output which way is
`better` and the bounds every value lies within, both inclusive, on a
`programs` port the `inputs` each program takes and the `outputs` the
primitive gives of each, and a sentence saying what it takes or gives
back, none when the primitive gives none. The `outcome` port may carry
`outcomes`: each outcome the step can report, in the declaration's
order, with a line saying when (`accepted`: "the source compiles"), for
the step's drawer to say what it reports; none when the primitive does
not say, and on every other port.
PrimitivePort.title: PrimitivePort

Problem.description: Extra members are allowed: `sole_admin` carries `scopes`, for instance.
Problem.title: Problem

PublicAnswer.description:
A public answer: the announcement every entrant reads, and the
question as it now stands, with the message naming it.
PublicAnswer.title: PublicAnswer

PublicAnswerRequest.description:
An answer made public: the announcement's title and text, and
whether to mark the question answered, as a reply's "Mark it answered"
does; it is unless `mark` is false.
PublicAnswerRequest.title: PublicAnswerRequest

PublicContest.description:
A public contest `where` it is, by the names of its org and itself,
with its title as `name`, what it says of itself and when it runs.
`tasks` are its released tasks, and empty in the list of contests.
PublicContest.title: PublicContest

PublicStatement.description: A released task of a public contest with its statement in Markdown.
PublicStatement.title: PublicStatement

PublicTask.description:
A released task of a public contest: its name, the label the contest
gives it, and its title.
PublicTask.title: PublicTask

Publication.description:
One publication: its number among the task's publications, the version
it froze, whether it changed how the task grades and what, and when.
Which workflow each of its
workflow names was at the forge stays out. `check` is where its save's
check stands, null once it passed or on a task that is not checked;
once it is `refused`, `failed_checks` lists each of the task's checks
that did not get what it expects, empty otherwise.
Publication.title: Publication

Published.description:
A save that published: the new publication's number among the task's,
whether it changed how the task grades, and what, the notes the save
makes of the task beside publishing it, how many submissions it
`regraded`, queued to be graded again against it, and what it did,
`effect`, in the words the question before a save in a running contest
uses. `check` is `checking` while the new publication is checked before
it takes over, as is a save of the same files that checks a refused one
again. `regrade` is the regrade the save started, whose summary the
task's regrades read, null when it started none now: a task checked
first starts its regrade once the check passes.
Published.title: Published

PutBack.description:
A withdrawn task put back: what each leaderboard reports of its tasks now,
as a save of the contest's settings answers.
PutBack.title: PutBack

QuestionRequest.description:
A question's title and text, and the name of the task it is about,
when it is about one released to the asker.
QuestionRequest.title: QuestionRequest

QueueDepth.description:
How many of a contest's gradings wait: for a machine, `queued`, whose
run is not started yet, and `dispatched`, whose run the CI holds until a
machine takes it; and for staff, `failed`, the latest attempts of
submissions that read as a system error.
QueueDepth.title: QueueDepth

QueueRow.description:
A row in a task's grading queue: whose it is, when the task closed
for it, its extension included, and the submissions to the task its
cells counted, oldest first.
QueueRow.title: QueueRow

QueuedMark.description:
One of the task's `entered` values and the submission's mark for it,
null while none is entered.
QueuedMark.title: QueuedMark

QueuedSubmission.description:
A submission a row's cells counted: its number, each cell that
counted it, and each of the task's `entered` values with its mark, in
the task's order.
QueuedSubmission.title: QueuedSubmission

Rate.description: At most `count` submissions in any `per` seconds.
Rate.title: Rate

Reader.description: Someone a workflow is shared with, by their username.
Reader.title: Reader

Refusal.description:
Why the caller cannot register now: the code registering would be
refused with, or `forge_unavailable` when their addresses could not be
checked just now, and its sentence.
Refusal.title: Refusal

RegisterRequest.description:
The new entrant's name, needed when the contest's entrants may be more
than one person and refused when they are one each, and the code a
sign-up asks for, when the caller is asked for one.
RegisterRequest.title: RegisterRequest

RegradeCause.description:
What started a regrade of many: staff's `rejudge` of the task, or the
`save` that published a change to how it grades.
RegradeCause.title: RegradeCause

RegradeChange.description:
What a regrade did to one submission: `change`, and the attempt
whose result it replaced, `earlier`, the one that counted when the
regrade began, null when there was none, beside its own attempt, `now`,
null while it has no result.

`regraded`, graded with an earlier result; `new`, graded with no earlier
result; `running`, still being graded; `failed`, no result yet, its
latest attempt a system error or cancelled; `over_limit`, not graded,
its entrant at the task's most submissions.
RegradeChange.title: RegradeChange

RegradeCounts.description: How many of a regrade's submissions each change counts.
RegradeCounts.title: RegradeCounts

RegradeSummary.description:
A task's latest regrade of many as the contest's page shows it, "Regrade
of A: 120 graded": its id, the one the feed is read by; its task by name
and `label`, the letter of its place in the contest's `tasks`, null once
the contest no longer lists it; what started it, `cause`, a staff
`rejudge` or the `save` that published `publication`, the publication
its attempts grade against; when and by whom, by user id and
`started_by_name`, their username, null when the forge does not say; how
many submissions it took, `total`; how many it `graded`, finishing with
a result (`regraded` and `new` together); whether any is still
`running`; and `counts`, by change. It stays until a newer regrade of
the task replaces it or a manager of the task dismisses it.
RegradeSummary.title: RegradeSummary

RejectRequest.description: Why, in words the entrant's members read on their own page.
RejectRequest.title: RejectRequest

Rejudged.description:
What a rejudge did: the publication the new attempts grade against,
how many it queued, how many unfinished attempts against an older
publication it cancelled first, how many it left to finish against
the current one, how many delayed submissions it ended `over_limit`,
their entrants at the task's most submissions, and `regrade`, the
regrade of many it is kept as, null when it made no attempt.
Rejudged.title: Rejudged

Result.description:
The attempt of a submission's grading that counts, as its contestant
sees it: the latest that finished with a result, as the leaderboards
count it, so a regrade under way, a failure or a cancel leaves the
result as it was, and while none has, the latest. Its id, attempt and
status, in the contestant's words: `queued` until its run is started,
`grading` while it is graded, `graded` once it has a result, `delayed`
while it has none and its grading failed on the platform's side,
`over_limit` once it was to be graded again with no room left under the
task's most submissions, and `cancelled` once staff end it; organisers
read the grading's own status in the gradings routes. A `delayed` one
carries nothing else: it is tried again once by itself, and then waits
for staff, who grade it again or end it: then it is `cancelled`, with
`reason`, the sentence they gave, which is null on every other status. A
delayed one is graded again only while its
entrant's submissions with a result, those waiting that are not
delayed, and the delayed ones made before it are fewer than the task's
most, so the first ones to get a result count, and otherwise it is
`over_limit`, with `limit`,
the most it reached ("Not graded: you had reached the limit of 10
submissions for this task."), and nothing else; `limit` is null on every
other status.

`run_values` holds each value of its scoring its entrant is shown,
worked out on every read, and `runs` the runs, those listed under `now` from the start,
those under `after_close` once the task reveals, and those under
`on_release` while staff have released the task's results, hidden
again when they take the release back. `once` holds what its steps
done once reported, and what a batch step gives once for all its runs,
that `show` lists, the compile log among them when listed, once a run
is shown; and `compiled` 1, or 0 when the entrant's code did not
compile, from the time `show` lists it or once a run is shown, null
while its compile is still to run. A task with
nothing shown during the contest is `submitted` until the reveal, which
a page words "Submitted, results after the contest". After the reveal,
while its late runs are still being graded, it is `grading` or
`delayed`. A grading whose runs failed for the platform is `delayed`
with the runs it gave, a value reading one of its failed early runs
`waiting`. `reveal_at` is when the task reveals, until then, as what its
entrant reads changes then with no grading's change to say so, so a page
open on it reads it again then; null once it has revealed.
Result.title: Result

Results.description:
Where a task's results stand: whether they are released now, showing
every entrant what the task's `show` lists under `on_release`, and every
release and take-back, oldest first.
Results.title: Results

ResultsAction.description:
One staff action on a task's results: `released` or `hidden_again`,
by whom, by user id and `by_name`, their username, null when the forge
does not say, and when.
ResultsAction.title: ResultsAction

ResultsRequest.description:
A release of a task's results or a take-back. Without `confirm`
nothing changes, and the answer is `confirmation_required` with the
words to show.
ResultsRequest.title: ResultsRequest

RollbackFile.description:
Write the file as it was at `version` back as a new change, `token`
being the one of the file as it is now, and, for a task, `confirm`,
`asked` and `keep_as_draft` doing what they do for a save.
RollbackFile.title: RollbackFile

RowDiff.description:
One row of a leaderboard before the regrade and after: whose it is, its
place on each side, null on a leaderboard with no `sort` or, before, for a
row that had none, its displayed cells, and its submissions of the
task the regrade is still grading, whose earlier result the after
side reads until it ends.
RowDiff.title: RowDiff

RunRegradeSummary.description:
A regrade by what it changed: its `id`, what started it,
the publication it grades against, how many submissions it took,
`total`, how many are still `running`, how many ended with no
result, `failed`, and how many it cannot compare, `unread`, since
the publication their result counted under no longer reads;
`changed`, each submission whose values or verdicts it changed, old
to new, in the order they were made, at most 100, with `more_changed`
counting the rest, an attempt compared with the one that counted when
the regrade began, both worked out as organisers read them, the
extensions and marks as they stand now; and `leaderboards`, each leaderboard that reads the
task before and after, given to a manager or admin of the contest
alone, null for anyone else.
RunRegradeSummary.title: RunRegradeSummary

RunShown.description:
One run of a grading as its entrant sees it: the group
`show` lists that shows it, its place in that group from 1 ("Test 3"),
one tuple per axis, its verdict, `passed`, 1 when that is `accepted`,
the numbers its steps reported, each by its title and unit, exactly,
and its texts, with the `label` and `message` shown with its verdict,
null when no step wrote one. A run in two groups shown is shown in
each; a run no group shown holds is never shown, even when a value
shown reads it. Organisers read every run, under `all` in the task's
order, with its `id`, which counts every run of the task; `id` is null
for an entrant. A run a row holds that the task's latest publication no
longer has is `dropped`, listed to organisers after the rest; never to
an entrant.
RunShown.title: RunShown

RunTuple.description:
One axis of a run: its title, null when that tuple has none, and the
columns of that axis the reader is shown, a file left out until `show`
lists it.
RunTuple.title: RunTuple

RunValue.description:
One value of a task's scoring as its reader sees it: its name,
its `number`, exact, null when it is missing, waiting or text; its
`text`, null when it is a number, missing or waiting; whether
it is `waiting` for staff, which an entrant reads as "being checked",
told only once the runs it waits on are early or shown; and whether it
is `self_reported`, reading a column the entrant could set. Organisers
also read the time `show` lists it under, null when never, and what it
read: `runs` by id, `values` and `facts`; each is null for an entrant.
RunValue.title: RunValue

RunVerdict.description:
One run of a grading: its id and key as the plan gives
them, its verdict, 1 `passed` when that is `accepted`, the numbers its
steps reported, exactly, and the texts, with the label and message
shown with the verdict, null when no step wrote one.
RunVerdict.title: RunVerdict

RunsResult.description:
A grading's result, version 6, one per pipeline: each run
it grades with its verdict, what the steps done once reported, what
staff alone see, and, when a run's verdict is `system_error`, the
sentence for staff saying why. Where its log went stays out.
RunsResult.title: RunsResult

SaveDefinition.description:
A draft to write over the one read with `token`, or to create when
the token is none. `changes` writes its own files in the same commit.
Whatever it holds saves, problems and all.
SaveDefinition.title: SaveDefinition

SaveEffect.description:
What a save does, in the words and parts a running contest's
`confirmation_required` asks with: `summary`, "Results change." or
"Nobody's result changes.", with `results_change` its flag; and the
sentences under "Runs again", "Scores" and "What entrants read", each
list holding at least one, a "nothing changes" line when nothing does.
SaveEffect.title: SaveEffect

SaveRequest.description:
The files a save writes, several at once. `keep_as_draft` writes them
as a draft that says what it held back and publishes nothing, on any
save. Otherwise, while the task's contest runs, `confirm` publishes a
save, which every save that would publish something new needs then; an
empty save with `confirm` publishes a draft kept earlier. `asked` is the
`confirmation_required`'s own: with it, the confirmation stands only
while the head and the latest publication are the ones asked about.
SaveRequest.title: SaveRequest

ScopeNames.description:
The names of the org, the contest and the task a scope reaches, as far
down as it does, in the shape of an address: `acme`, `acme/spring`,
`acme/spring/sum`.
ScopeNames.title: ScopeNames

SelfReported.description: A value a column reads that reads a column the entrant could set.
SelfReported.title: SelfReported

SessionInfo.description:
One place this user is signed in, described by its device and its
times. The address a session came from is kept for the record and stays
out of the answer.
SessionInfo.title: SessionInfo

SetVisibility.description:
Private, shared or public. Private and public empty the list of
readers; shared keeps it.
SetVisibility.title: SetVisibility

ShownOutput.description:
One number a run reported, named by the title its workflow gives it,
or by its own name, with its unit, null when it has none, and the
number exactly.
ShownOutput.title: ShownOutput

Slot.description:
A slot for one file: where to send it, and when the slot stops being
good. `ready` is true for a file the forge already holds, which is sent
again by sending nothing.
Slot.title: Slot

SortKey.description:
A column rows are sorted by, in turn: `desc` puts the highest first,
`asc` the lowest, and a row with no number comes after every row with
one.
SortKey.title: SortKey

StaffNote.description:
What a step wrote for staff alone, for one run or, `run` null, once:
its message to staff and its extras, each null when it wrote none.
StaffNote.title: StaffNote

Submission.description:
One of the caller's submissions of the task: its number among them,
when it was taken, and its grading.
Submission.title: Submission

SubmissionChange.description:
One submission a regrade changed: its latest attempt of the regrade,
`grading`, which the task's gradings read in full, the submission by
`number`, each value it changed, and the runs whose verdict it changed,
at most 20 listed and `more_verdicts` counting the rest.
SubmissionChange.title: SubmissionChange

SubmissionState.description:
Where a submission stands as its contestant is told, in TASK-FORMAT.md
section 1.7's words, which say nothing of the CI's stages: `queued`
until its run is started, `grading` while the CI holds it or runs it,
`graded` once it has a result, `delayed` while it has none and its
latest attempt failed for a reason of the platform's, `over_limit` once
it was to be graded again and its entrant had no room left under the
task's `submissions.max`, and `cancelled` once staff ended it. A run
task's submission with no run shown during the contest is `submitted`
once graded and until the task reveals, which a page words "Submitted,
results after the contest", since `graded` would read as nothing run.
SubmissionState.title: SubmissionState

Submissions.description:
What a submit is counted against: at most `max` submissions in all,
and at most `rate` of them in any window.
Submissions.title: Submissions

SubmitRequest.description:
A submit: `idempotency_key` is 8 to 128 letters, digits, `-` and `_`,
made once by the browser for this submit, so sending it again answers
with the submission it made and makes nothing. `inputs` is keyed by the
id of each of the task's contestant inputs, and forge checks them
against the task's inputs; a value left out takes its default.
SubmitRequest.title: SubmitRequest

SubmittedFileInput.description:
What one input of a submission was: the paths of its files in the
submission, each a download through the download door, or the value
given, a number as its exact decimal digits; or, for an input given
once per tuple, its `parts` by number from "1", only the parts given,
its own `files` empty and `value` null, and `parts` null on any other.
It is read leniently from the submission's `submission.json`: a member
of the wrong type is left out rather than failing the answer.
SubmittedFileInput.title: SubmittedFileInput

SubmittedFiles.description: What a submission was made with, by input id.
SubmittedFiles.title: SubmittedFiles

SubmittedInput.description:
What a contestant gives for one input: the uploads of its files; or,
for a text, number, true-or-false or enum input, its value. A number is
given as the text of its plain decimal digits, `2.5`, the form every
number is served in, so it is checked and written exactly, never read
into a float on the way.
SubmittedInput.title: SubmittedInput

SubmittedPart.description:
What one part of an input given in parts was: the paths of its files
in the submission, each a download through the download door, or the
value given, a number as its exact decimal digits. It is read leniently
from the submission's `submission.json`: a member of the wrong type is
left out rather than failing the answer.
SubmittedPart.title: SubmittedPart

Submitter.description:
Whose a submission is, as an organiser recognises it: the entrant, by
its id and the name it is shown under, none once it is gone; and the
member who submitted it, by user id and username, none when a reconcile
found it at the forge, the username none when the forge did not say.
Submitter.title: Submitter

TakeOut.description:
What taking a task out of its contest does: `remove` it, while nobody
has submitted to it, or `withdraw` it, once anyone has.
TakeOut.title: TakeOut

TakeOutRequest.description:
What taking a task out of its contest should do, as the organiser
confirmed it: `remove` or `withdraw`, as the task list's `take_out`
said when the dialog asked.
TakeOutRequest.title: TakeOutRequest

TakenOut.description: What taking the task out did: `remove`d it or `withdraw`n it.
TakenOut.title: TakenOut

TaskEntry.description:
A task released to the caller: its name, the label its place in the
contest gives it, its title, whether they may submit to it now, and
when it falls due, null when it has no due, and closes for them, their
extension on it included. A task's standing on the contest's leaderboards is the
leaderboards' own to say, the home's `standing` among them.
TaskEntry.title: TaskEntry

TaskFileUploadRequest.description:
One file an organiser puts into the task: the `path` it goes to in the
task's files, its size in bytes, the SHA-256 of its content in lowercase
hex and, when the browser knows it, its content type.
TaskFileUploadRequest.title: TaskFileUploadRequest

TaskPage.description:
A task as the caller reads it: its statement in Markdown, the caps a
submit is counted against, the inputs a contestant gives, when it falls
due and closes for them, and `marks`, how many of their entrant's
submissions they may mark, null unless the contest's entry for the
task gives `marks` or a leaderboard reads which of the task's
submissions an entrant marks, and their entrant is approved; and
nothing else the task holds.
TaskPage.title: TaskPage

TaskRelease.description:
Whether the task is released, visible and open to one person now, and
when it is not open, the first reason why.
TaskRelease.title: TaskRelease

TaskStanding.description:
One task of a contest as its organisers work from it: the task by
name, its letter by its place in the contest's `tasks`, where its files
stand as `GET <task>` gives it, and its timeline from its entry, each
time at its default where the entry gives none: `release_at`, `due`,
null on a task with no due, and `closes`.

`withdrawn` says the task is withdrawn from the contest: it keeps its
place and its letter, entrants do not see it and no leaderboard counts
it, until it is put back. `submissions` is how many submissions it has,
any entrant's, and `take_out` what taking it out of the contest would
do, for the dialog that asks first: `remove`, while it has none, which
deletes it, or `withdraw`, once it has; null while it is withdrawn,
when it can only be put back.
TaskStanding.title: TaskStanding

TaskState.description:
Where a task's files stand: the version at their head, the latest
publication or none, and whether the head is a draft, a state no
publication froze. A draft carries the errors that keep it from
publishing; a draft with none was held back, or has not been saved since
it was made. `statement_written` says whether the latest publication
holds a statement, there, not blank and not the starter's placeholder,
false when nothing is published, and `head_statement_written` the same
of the head. `results` says where the task's results stand.
TaskState.title: TaskState

TextRef.description:
A text a step wrote, read apart and only while the result shows it.
Organisers are told the stored output that holds it and that output's
name, and read it by them. An entrant is told neither, both null, since
the output may be another entrant's and its id says when it was made:
they read it by where it is shown, its run's group and place, or
neither for what is given once, and the text's name or `label` or
`message`.
TextRef.title: TextRef

Timeline.description:
A task's timeline in its contest, from its entry in `contest.yaml`,
each at its default where the entry gives none: `release_at`, the
contest's start unless the entry says; `due`, after which a submission
is late, none unless the entry says; and `closes`, the contest's end
unless the entry says.
Timeline.title: Timeline

TreeEntry.description:
One entry of a folder: a file, with the size of what its commit
holds and that commit, the one that last changed it, which holds it as
listed whatever the head has moved to since (none when the forge does
not say), or a folder. `upload` tells an uploaded file from a typed one.
`token` is the file's `ConflictToken`, as a read gives it, plain text so the
entry is served as it is; `start` is how a small text
file begins (`start_of`), none for any other file and for an upload,
whose commit holds only the pointer to its bytes.
TreeEntry.title: TreeEntry

UpdateOrg.description: The org's description, and its display name when given.
UpdateOrg.title: UpdateOrg

Upload.description:
Where one upload stands: the input it is for, empty for a file an
organiser puts into the task, its name and content type, the size and
digest declared for it, and its status. `verified` is an upload a submit
or a save may name.
Upload.title: Upload

UploadInfo.description:
What a file that is an upload holds: the size and SHA-256 of the
bytes the forge's large-file store keeps for it. Its commit holds the
pointer to them, which is what `content` and `size` describe, so it is
never opened as text, and it is changed by uploading it again.
UploadInfo.title: UploadInfo

UploadRequest.description:
One file to upload for the task's contestant input `input`: where it
goes under the input, one name for a file input and a path of names for
a folder input; its size in bytes, the SHA-256 of its content in
lowercase hex and, when the browser knows it, its content type.

The digest is what the forge checks the bytes against as they arrive, so
a file that changed between being read and being sent is refused there
rather than committed.
UploadRequest.title: UploadRequest

UploadStatus.description:
Where an upload stands: `waiting` until the forge holds its bytes,
`verified` once the forge says it does, and `consumed` once a commit
holds the pointer to it.
UploadStatus.title: UploadStatus

ValueChange.description:
One value of a submission a regrade changed: its `name`, its
number `before` and `after`, exactly, null where it had none, waits
or is text; its text `text_before` and `text_after`, null where it
had no text; and whether it is `waiting` after, for a run or for
staff. A value has
no direction: up and down are a row's place on a leaderboard.
ValueChange.title: ValueChange

VerdictChange.description:
One run whose verdict a regrade changed, by id, its verdict
`before` and `after`, null where the grading did not hold the run; or,
with `run` null, every one of the submission's `runs` runs, each of
which changed from the same verdict to the same other one.
VerdictChange.title: VerdictChange

WayKind.description:
How a member came into their entrant: by the contest's invite way, by
one of its sign-ups, or put there by an organiser.
WayKind.title: WayKind

Workflow.description: A workflow, by its owner and its name.
Workflow.title: Workflow

WorkflowBox.description:
A workflow version as a box. `run` is false for a workflow of the
test format, and then both lists are empty. `description` is what the
workflow says it does, or null when it says nothing.
WorkflowBox.title: WorkflowBox

WorkflowForm.description:
What the task form is built from: the workflow the task's `task.yaml`
names, as written, and the inputs it declares, in the order the
workflow gives them, or `problem`, the reason there are none: no
`task.yaml` or one that does not read as YAML, no workflow named, or one
that cannot be read or is in an old form; `graded`, whether the task has
a graded submission; and `newer`, the workflow's latest version when it
comes after the one the task names, which the task keeps until someone
saves it naming another (Task 10.6.5). `text_values` names the values
that give text, in the file's order, none when the settings cannot be
read; a workflow output stays a number.
WorkflowForm.title: WorkflowForm

WorkflowItem.description:
A workflow a person may read: its visibility, its versions in natural
order, and whether they may edit it.
WorkflowItem.title: WorkflowItem

WorkflowPage.title: WorkflowPage

WriteFile.description:
One file written, `token` being the one it was read with or null for
a new file. For a task this is a save, and `confirm`, `asked` and
`keep_as_draft` do what they do for one.
WriteFile.title: WriteFile

WriteTaskFile.description:
One file of a task written, as a save: typed content or an upload
made for this path, `token` being the one it was read with or null for
a new file, and `confirm`, `asked` and `keep_as_draft` doing what they
do for a save.

Written.description:

get.description:
At most `limit` gradings of the contest's tasks the caller observes,
newest first, every attempt a row of its own, so a submission graded
again shows more than once, or, with `latest`, only each submission's
latest attempt. One whose run is overdue or lost reads as
`system_error` with the reason, and a filter by status takes it as it
reads, so `status=system_error&latest=true` gives the failed gradings
the queue's `failed` counts. A task, username or entrant the contest does not have, or a task
the caller does not observe, gives no rows; a username that breaks the
forge's rule for one is a `validation_error`.

With `regrade`, the regrade of many a summary of `/gradings/regrades`
names, it lists that regrade's gradings, one per submission, its latest
attempt of the regrade, newest first, each with `change`, what it did
to the submission beside the result it replaced, the earlier attempt
and its own by number; `change` narrows them to one kind, and `user` and
`entrant` narrow as ever, while `task`, `status` and `latest` are not
read with it. A regrade the caller cannot see gives no rows, and so
does `change` without `regrade`.
